subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: Find the angle between the curves y² = 8x and 4x² + y² = 32.

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IB (2026-27 edition), book p.217, chapter 10 APPLICATIONS OF DERIVATIVES, the TANGENTS AND NORMALS sub-section, Short Answer question 5(ii). recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — say how you find where the curves meet, which root you reject and why, and what formula gives the angle.

steps.label: Find the point of intersection
steps.margin_note: Two marks. Substituting y² = 8x into the ellipse leaves a quadratic in x alone. The root x = −4 must be rejected in writing, with the reason: y² = 8x forces x ≥ 0.
lines: From (i), y² = 8x ≥ 0, so x cannot be negative. Reject x = −4.
∴ the curves meet at P(2, 4) and at (2, −4). Work at P(2, 4).

recall.must_convey: That substituting y² = 8x into the ellipse gives x² + 2x − 8 = 0, x = 2 (rejecting x = −4), so the point is (2, 4).

steps.why: The angle between two curves is the angle between their tangents at a point they share, so the shared point must be found before any differentiation. Dividing 4x² + 8x = 32 through by 4 first keeps the numbers small.
common_mistakes: Keeping x = −4 and finding an angle at a point that does not exist on the parabola.
Forgetting to divide by 4 and mis-factorising 4x² + 8x − 32 = 0.
Taking y = ±4 but then using x = −4 as the y-value.
steps.memory_tip: A parabola y² = 4ax lives only on one side of the y-axis, so any negative x from the algebra is not on the curve.

steps.label: Find both slopes there
steps.margin_note: Third mark. Differentiate each curve implicitly, then substitute (2, 4). The 4 in 4x² becomes 8x, which is where the slope −4x/y comes from.

recall.must_convey: That m₁ = 4/y = 1 for the parabola and m₂ = −4x/y = −2 for the ellipse at (2, 4).

steps.why: Each curve has its own tangent at the shared point, so two separate derivatives are needed. Substituting the point only after differentiating keeps both slopes correct.
common_mistakes: Writing the ellipse slope as −x/y, which is the circle formula, not this one.
Substituting x = 2 and y = 4 into the curve before differentiating.
steps.memory_tip: For any curve Ax² + By² = C the slope is −Ax/(By) — the circle case A = B = 1 is just the simplest example.

steps.label: Apply the angle formula
steps.margin_note: Last mark. Here 1 + m₁m₂ = −1, so the fraction is negative before the modulus is taken. The modulus is what keeps the acute angle.
lines: If θ is the angle between the curves at P, then

recall.must_convey: That tanθ = |(m₁ − m₂)/(1 + m₁m₂)| = |3/(−1)| = 3, so θ = Tan⁻¹3.

steps.why: A negative value inside the modulus only means the difference of the two direction angles is obtuse. Taking the modulus reports the acute angle, which is the standard answer.
common_mistakes: Reporting θ = Tan⁻¹(−3) and giving an obtuse angle.
Writing 1 − m₁m₂ in the denominator instead of 1 + m₁m₂.
Cancelling the 3 and the −1 into −3 and then squaring it.
steps.memory_tip: Difference on top, one plus the product underneath, modulus around the whole fraction.
